subject: SparkBridge — purchase-onboarding flow & payment constraints
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@sparkbridge.com>, Tim Chu <tim.chu@sparkbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: SparkBridge discovery — quick recap & payment questions

Thanks for the time today — quick recap from our call and a couple of narrow asks so we can model the commercial path. TL;DR: SparkBridge is a great fit for a 6–8 week pilot; procurement path will determine whether we can start on-card or need a PO-first engagement.

Call highlights
- Pilot scope: 3 internal teams (search + support + analytics), up to 200k token/month.
- Security: you confirmed SOC2 in-scope; security team wants the SOC2 report and a contact for a short questionnaire.
- Procurement needs: primary AP policy is Net30 PO for recurring SaaS; card acceptance possible for pilots under internal threshold (see below).

Open questions / asks for procurement team (Lena / Tim)
1) Thresholds: what is the current card threshold (single purchase and annual)? You mentioned there’s a $10k single-charge cap for smaller pilots but I want this in writing.
2) Marketplace preference: are you able to transact via AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace? If yes, that simplifies vendor onboarding for you.
3) Vendor docs: please confirm required onboarding docs (tax forms, W-9, COI, MSA redline window). I’ve attached our standard MSA (SparkBridge_MSA_v1.pdf) for review.

Suggested commercial path options (pick one):
A) Card-first pilot: pricing kept under $10k (one-time card payment) → transition to PO for annual commit. Fastest (3–5 business days).
B) PO-first pilot: submit PO and run pilot under Net30 terms. Add 7–10 business days for vendor setup.
C) Marketplace purchase: immediate checkout and standard marketplace billing; depends on marketplace availability.

Immediate next steps
- Lena: confirm thresholds and list of mandatory vendor docs.
- Tim: confirm if IT will allow marketplace procurement (I can loop in our marketplace ops).
- Marissa / Karthik (cc): if we decide card-first, can you draft a one-page commercial summary and a pilot SOW under $10k?

Attachments: SparkBridge_MSA_v1.pdf (MSA stub)

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Jul 12, 2028 at 2:05 PM, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the time today — quick recap from our call and a couple of narrow asks so we can model the commercial path. TL;DR: SparkBridge is a great fit for a 6–8 week pilot; procurement path will determine whether we can start on-card or need a PO-first engagement.

Thanks Sean — helpful summary. A few clarifications from procurement: 
- Card thresholds: Finance permits credit card purchases up to $10,000 single-charge and $25,000 annual cap per vendor for new vendors. Anything above requires a Net30 PO + vendor onboarding.
- PO timeline: Expect vendor setup + PO issuance in ~7–12 business days once legal/tax docs are provided.
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace purchases where possible (reduces vendor risk), but IT needs to confirm whether AWS Marketplace is allowed for this product — I’ll check and loop back.
- Required docs: W-9, COI, standard MSA (we typically redline within a week). We’ll also need the SOC2 or an equivalent security questionnaire completed.

Action items for our side:
- I’ll confirm the marketplace OK/no-go by EOD Thu (Jul 14).
- If we go card route, Tim will give me a short PO fallback contact for AP.

Happy to run this in whichever path gets you fastest to a pilot.

—Lena
Lena Ortiz

Quick internal note and a proposed tactic:

Sean — I can prepare a one-page commercial summary plus a pilot SOW that keeps the first-month spend under $10k so SparkBridge’s procurement can approve a card payment immediately. I’m attaching a very short pricing sheet (pilot-pricing-sheet.pdf) with two options:
- Option 1 (Card-friendly pilot): $9,750 flat for 4 weeks (includes standard support, onboarding assistance).
- Option 2 (Pilot with extended token cap): $14,500 for 6 weeks — would trigger PO requirement unless they stretch card threshold.

If Lena confirms marketplace is acceptable we’ll also prepare the marketplace SKU mapping (faster vendor ops). Otherwise, Option 1 lets us start in ~48 hours.

Thanks all — couple of quick notes from IT/Procurement ops: 
- Marketplace: IT confirms AWS Marketplace is permitted for commercial SaaS, but they need the marketplace listing ID from Redwood to validate entitlements.
- PO fallback: If we go PO-first, please include a vendor onboarding timeline in your SOW (we usually need the vendor contact, tax ID/EIN, W-9, COI).
- Single-sheet ask: Procurement would prefer a one-page commercial summary that lists pilot scope, cost, acceptance criteria, and proposed billing route (card vs PO vs marketplace). That accelerates approvals.

I’ll collect the formal vendor onboarding contact (AP contact + legal reviewer) and send separately — target by EOD Thu.
